_meta.description: Adaptive-capacity / transition-strategy layer. Converts Layer-2 GROSS revenue erosion (a frozen company losing its incumbent product demand) into RESIDUAL risk after a stated transition pathway, given where the company starts. Three levers: ambition (how much it pivots, defaulted from the scenario narrative), positioning (how well-placed it is today — 'science' derived from emissions + lever readiness + plan strength, with an 'art' override), and transition capex (the cost of the pivot, company-provided or estimated with a geographic buffer).
_meta.non_duplication_note: Capture reduces the REVENUE-erosion lens (cash flow); positioning reduces the STRANDING lens (balance sheet, separate); transition capex is a NEW cash-flow cost representing the investment that earns the capture. Each routes once.
sources: BSR, 'Decarbonization Lever Library: Mapped Sectoral Transition Pathways' (Nov 2025) — the 'business transformation / systemic adaptability over 10-20-30-year horizons' framing (pp. 9, 15, 18) and sector lever-maturity pathways inform positioning (lever readiness) and the scenario-narrative ambition mapping.
Scenario ambition mapped to NGFS Phase V narrative intent (orderly vs disorderly vs hot-house).
Pivot-capex ratios: order-of-magnitude sector transformation capex (IEA NZE sectoral investment, Mission Possible Partnership transition strategies).
Geographic buffer: relative execution/financing cost by NGFS region band.

scenario_ambition._note: Default company pivot ambition [0,1] implied by each scenario's narrative. Orderly/ambitious scenarios pull companies into an aggressive pivot; hot-house scenarios imply little transition. Overridable per company. Rationale: Way, Ives, Mealy & Farmer (2022, Joule) show a fast clean-energy transition is the LOW-COST path (clean tech on exponential decline, fossil flat), so under ambitious scenarios the rational firm response is a strong pivot — the ambition defaults encode that.

maturity_readiness._note: Decarb-lever commercial maturity → adaptability score. A sector whose primary levers are mature/cheap is easier to pivot than one dependent on frontier tech.

positioning._note: Weights for the derived 'science' positioning score P in [0,1] (higher = better placed). plan_coverage is the share of the sector's PRIMARY levers the company has in its transition plan (from the Lever Library overlay); passed in by the app, else falls back to plan_strength.

target_year_to_plan_strength._note: decarb_target_year → plan-strength component. No target = weak; earlier net-zero = stronger. Interpolated between anchors; residual % scales it down.

positioning._already_note: A perfectly-positioned firm (P=1) is assumed to have already transitioned up to this share of its incumbent base, so it strands that much less.

capture._note: Capture fraction of gross erosion that the company offsets by pivoting = ambition × positioning_effectiveness, capped by the opportunity ceiling (how much the challenger/green market is growing). positioning_effectiveness bends the raw P slightly so a mid score is a bit below linear.
capture._ceiling_note: opportunity ceiling = challenger-market growth headroom; never below opportunity_ceiling_floor so some pivot is always possible.

transition_capex._note: Model estimate when the company does not provide a planned capex. capex ≈ ambition × replacement_value × sector_pivot_capex_ratio × region_multiplier × positioning_capex_factor. Poorly-positioned firms pay more per unit pivoted.

sector_pivot_capex_ratio._note: Capex to fully pivot (ambition=1), as a fraction of the incumbent asset's replacement value.

region_multiplier._note: Geographic/context buffer on pivot cost (execution + financing risk). Advanced economies cheapest to execute; rest-of-world carries an execution premium.

positioning_capex_factor._note: Multiplier by positioning: a laggard (P→0) pays up to `poor`× the base; a mover (P→1) pays `strong`×. Linear in P.

phasing._note: Capex is spread over the pivot window (base_year → target_year, else 2050), front-loaded with a triangular profile peaking early.
